title: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients

fields.label: Label
fields.value: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the BETSE model of the Xenopus neurula, HCN2 channels open at hyperpolarized membrane voltage and hyperpolarize further when open, so they act as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small existing Vmem gradients: sufficiently negative neural tube cells go very hyperpolarized while depolarized lateral regions are left unchanged.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: HCN2 channels are predicted to open at hyperpolarized Vmem, generating more hyperpolarization with opening, thereby serving as a Vmem-controlled switch of Vmem state, capable of amplifying small Vmem gradients, similar to IT effect (Fig. 3c, e, f).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent”. Scope: BETSE bioelectric model of an anterior stage-15 Xenopus neurula

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a quantitative simulation claim with explicit channel behavior, geometry, and expected output. Public simulation software and the paper's parameter specification should permit reproduction and robustness testing within weeks.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reimplement or rerun the specified BETSE neurula model with and without HCN2, sweep initial Vmem gradients, and test whether HCN2 activation steepens the neural-to-lateral voltage difference while leaving depolarized regions nearly unchanged.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exact paper-specific configuration files may not be deposited.

Results may depend on assumed HCN2 kinetics and ionic medium.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a statement about a specified model, and both the engine and the HCN2 kinetics are public. Table 1, the regional leak ratios, and the permeability ratio are enough for a small team to rerun the qualitative switch in weeks. Channelpedia independently fixes the activation range, so a failure to amplify is evidence about the model rather than a missing parameter file. Residual uncertainty is the unpublished YAML, which can change millivolts and is unlikely to flip the sign of the switch inside the published ranges.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In a BETSE neurula with the published leak ratios, 0.1× MMR ions, and HCN2 at Na+:K+ permeability 0.2, compare open probability and steady Vmem in the neural tube versus the lateral regions. Amplification is confirmed if already-negative tube cells hyperpolarize further while depolarized lateral cells stay near their baseline; a uniform shift, or depolarization on HCN2 opening, refutes the switch.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The cAMP shift of V1/2 is an assumption (+20 mV) rather than a fitted embryonic measurement.

The exact simulation YAML is not in the repository and must be rebuilt from the supplement.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In a coupled-cell bioelectric model of the anterior stage-15 Xenopus neurula built with the paper's stated ingredients (Table 1 concentrations, 0.1x MMR medium, three regions whose K+/Cl- leak differences give a hyperpolarized neural tube near -50 mV and lateral neural folds/ectoderm near -5 mV, Kir channels, voltage-sensitive gap junctions) and BETSE's HCN2 kinetic model (V1/2 = -99 mV shifted +20 mV by cAMP, Na+:K+ permeability 0.2), adding homogeneously expressed HCN2 opens it preferentially in the hyperpolarized tube, drives tube cells further negative, and leaves the depolarized lateral regions essentially unchanged, i.e. it amplifies the existing Vmem gradient rather than shifting all regions uniformly.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered, evaluated at the primary HCN2 expression level (the paper's/BETSE's stated HCN2 maximum permeability if recoverable from Table 1, the Supplementary Note or a published BETSE config; otherwise the BETSE default for its HCN2 channel class) in the three-region coupled sheet calibrated so the HCN2-free control gives tube Vmem within -50 +/- 10 mV and lateral Vmem within -5 +/- 5 mV: ALL of (a) the GHK reversal potential of HCN2 current under Table 1 cytosol and 0.1x MMR is more negative than the control tube Vmem; (b) tube Vmem with HCN2 minus control tube Vmem <= -15 mV; (c) the largest absolute change in mean Vmem of either lateral region <= 5 mV; (d) the lateral-minus-tube Vmem difference increases by >= 15 mV; (e) steady-state HCN2 open probability in the tube is >= 5 times that in the ectoderm. Secondary (switch/amplification): in uncoupled single cells whose control Vmem is swept from about -70 to 0 mV by varying K+ leak, the HCN2-induced shift is >= 15 mV in magnitude for some cells with control Vmem <= -40 mV and <= 5 mV for all cells with control Vmem >= -15 mV, and the expression range (log sweep 0.01x to 100x the primary level) over which (b)-(d) all hold spans at least one decade.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: any of (i) HCN2 reversal potential more positive than the control tube Vmem (opening would depolarize the tube); (ii) tube shift > -5 mV at the primary expression level (no amplification); (iii) lateral shift magnitude >= half the tube shift magnitude at the primary level (near-uniform shift, not switch-like); (iv) no expression level in the 0.01x-100x sweep satisfies (b)-(d). Outcomes meeting neither the pass nor the fail criterion are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If the control calibration (tube -50 +/- 10, lateral -5 +/- 5 mV) cannot be achieved with Table 1 concentrations and the stated channel set, verdict is 'inconclusive' with reason 'other'.
